basic_information.official_title: AN ACT CREATING THE BANGSAMORO NUTRITION COMMISSION IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO, PROVIDING FOR ITS MANDATE, POWERS, AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
basic_information.approved_by: Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua — approved in December 2025; the day is handwritten on the signed copy and is not clearly legible in the captured scan, so the registry records the month only.
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation within the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates a Bangsamoro Nutrition Commission to lead the region's fight against hunger and malnutrition — with power to require data from any ministry and to make nutrition a scored criterion in local government awards.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The act treats nutritional improvement as the key component of human resource development, and sets out to build a mechanism for collaboration across agencies and sectors on hunger and malnutrition, especially for vulnerable groups.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A commission attached to the Office of the Chief Minister becomes the region's policy-making and coordinating body on food, nutrition and food security. Local governments must align their nutrition plans with the regional one and fold them into their investment programmes, and nutrition becomes a mandatory criterion in local governance awards.
who_will_be_affected: Children and families affected by hunger and malnutrition
Every LGU in the region, whose nutrition plans and staffing are now scored
Barangays, which are expected to recruit Barangay Nutrition Scholars
Ministries running feeding programmes, which must coordinate through the Commission
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force from 2026 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. The region has a Nutrition Commission that can demand data from any ministry, must align every LGU's nutrition plan with the regional one, and makes nutrition a scored criterion for local government awards.
in_practice: A Bangsamoro Nutrition Commission attached to the Office of the Chief Minister
A Board of Commissioners headed by a Chairperson who must be a nutrition expert, appointed by the Chief Minister for 6 years
Five ex officio members: the Ministers of Health; Basic, Higher and Technical Education; Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform; Interior and Local Government; and Social Services and Development
It leads the Bangsamoro Plan of Action for Nutrition and the Bangsamoro Food Security and Nutrition Plan
It may require submission of all necessary data, records and reports, and reports findings to the Chief Minister and Parliament
Every LGU's Local Nutrition Action Plan must be consistent with the regional plan and integrated into its Annual Investment Program
Nutrition becomes a mandatory criterion in local governance awards, scored on four indicators
₱15,000,000 initial, transferred directly to the Commission

for_specific_groups.Families facing hunger: The Commission is the region's coordinating body on food and nutrition, working with the ministries that run the Supplementary Feeding Program and the School-Based Feeding Program.
for_specific_groups.Local government units: Your nutrition plan must align with the regional plan and enter your Annual Investment Program. Four things are scored for governance awards: activating a Local Nutrition Committee, integrating the plan into your investment programme, recruiting Barangay Nutrition Scholars, and hiring a Registered Nutritionist-Dietitian as Nutrition Action Officer.
for_specific_groups.Nutritionists and dietitians: Section 13 pushes LGUs to hire a Registered Nutritionist-Dietitian as Nutrition Action Officer.
for_specific_groups.Barangays: Recruitment of Barangay Nutrition Scholars is one of the scored indicators.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The whole BARMM, including every local government unit.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Through local nutrition plans, feeding programmes and LGU staffing.
what_you_can_do: Ask your LGU whether its Local Nutrition Action Plan is in the Annual Investment Program
Ask whether your municipality has a Local Nutrition Committee and a Nutrition Action Officer
Ask the Commission for its periodic programmatic reviews — it must submit findings and recommendations to the Chief Minister and Parliament
watch_out_for: The Commission is a policy, coordinating and monitoring body — it does not itself deliver food or run feeding programmes.
The award indicators create pressure on LGUs but carry no penalty for failing them.
₱15 million is a floor for a region-wide mandate.

key_terms_explained.BPAN: Bangsamoro Plan of Action for Nutrition — the regional plan every local plan must align with.
key_terms_explained.BFSNP: Bangsamoro Food Security and Nutrition Plan.
key_terms_explained.LNAP: Local Nutrition Action Plan, prepared by each LGU.
key_terms_explained.AIP: Annual Investment Program — an LGU's yearly spending plan, which must now include the nutrition plan.
key_terms_explained.Barangay Nutrition Scholar: A community-level nutrition worker; recruiting them is one of the scored indicators.
key_terms_explained.Subsidiarity: The principle that decisions are made at the most local level capable of handling them — invoked here to align regional and national plans.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Jumada Al-Awwal 28, 1447 / 19 November 2025, approved by the Chief Minister in December 2025.

benefits.headline: A dedicated commission for hunger and malnutrition, with real leverage over local governments.

direct_benefits.benefit: A regional body coordinating food, nutrition and food security policy
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Everyone in the BARMM, especially vulnerable groups
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Through its policies, plans and programmatic reviews

direct_benefits.benefit: Local nutrition plans aligned to the regional plan and funded through LGU investment programmes
Nutrition staffing at local level — Nutrition Action Officers and Barangay Nutrition Scholars
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Scored under Section 13 in governance awards

direct_benefits.benefit: Findings and policy recommendations submitted to the Chief Minister and Parliament

indirect_benefits: Coordination with the Supplementary Feeding and School-Based Feeding Programs
Research on the state of food security and nutrition in the region
Authority to accept domestic and foreign grants
limitations: It coordinates and monitors; it does not deliver services.
No penalty attaches to the LGU indicators.

for_lgus: Keep your Local Nutrition Action Plan consistent with the Bangsamoro Plan of Action for Nutrition
Integrate the plan into your Annual Investment Program and pass the ordinances needed to implement it

for_ministries: Submit data, records and reports the Commission requires for its programmatic reviews

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts for the public and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.
penalties.note: The act relies on award criteria and reporting rather than sanctions to move local governments.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Bangsamoro Nutrition Commission, attached to the Office of the Chief Minister
where_to_complain.for_local_issues: Your LGU's Local Nutrition Committee and Nutrition Action Officer; the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government, which develops the assessment tools
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A parent asks why the school feeding programme is inconsistent. The Commission coordinates with the education ministry on the School-Based Feeding Program and with social services on the Supplementary Feeding Program, and can require data on how they are performing.

A municipality wants to win a local governance award. It must activate a Local Nutrition Committee, fold its nutrition plan into its investment programme, recruit Barangay Nutrition Scholars, and hire a Registered Nutritionist-Dietitian.
A researcher wants regional malnutrition data. The Commission leads research on the state of food security and nutrition and can require records from any ministry.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Nutrition Commission Act of 2025”.

Section 2 — Policy: nutritional improvement is the key component in human resource development; the Bangsamoro Government shall promote and protect access to adequate food and nutrition among all inhabitants, and establish a mechanism for collaboration and cooperation among agencies, sectors and stakeholders in addressing hunger and malnutrition, responsive to constituents and especially vulnerable groups.
Section 3 — Creates the Bangsamoro Nutrition Commission, attached to the Office of the Chief Minister.

Section 4 — A Board of Commissioners headed by a Chairperson, who must be a nutrition expert with wide experience of nutrition concerns in the BARMM, appointed by the Chief Minister for a six-year term subject to reappointment; five ex officio members — the Ministers of Health, of Basic, Higher and Technical Education, of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform, of the Interior and Local Government, and of Social Services and Development; and the Executive Director of the Commission Secretariat.

Section 5 — The Commission is the policy-making and coordinating body on food and nutrition, nutrition and health, and food security. It prescribes regional policies; coordinates planning, monitoring and evaluation of regional programmes including the private sector, conducting periodic in-depth programmatic reviews against the Bangsamoro Plan of Action for Nutrition, with authority to require submission of all necessary data, records and reports, and regularly submitting findings and policy recommendations to the Office of the Chief Minister and Parliament; promotes food security through education and public awareness; leads formulation of the BPAN and the Bangsamoro Food Security and Nutrition Plan; represents the region nationally; leads research; ensures all Local Nutrition Action Plans are consistent with the BPAN; strengthens stakeholder ownership through participation at every stage; may call on any ministry for personnel, facilities and resources; creates technical working committees; and may accept donations and grants from domestic or foreign sources.

Sections 6–9 — Organisational structure, a Secretariat headed by an Executive Director, and the Executive Director's qualifications: a Filipino citizen resident in the BARMM, at least 30 years old, of good moral character, a college graduate with at least 3 years' relevant experience in nutrition, public health administration or social services.

Section 11 — Coordination with the Ministry of Health on health policy, Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform on food security, the Interior and Local Government on local policy, Social Services and Development on the Supplementary Feeding Program, Basic, Higher and Technical Education on the School-Based Feeding Program, and Science and Technology on the innovation of complementary foods, along with other agencies and the LGUs.

Section 12 — In line with the principle of subsidiarity, regional nutrition plans are aligned with national plans and reference the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition. LGUs shall integrate their Local Nutrition Action Plan into their Annual Investment Programs and ensure implementation through appropriate programmes, policies and ordinances.

Section 13 — Consistent with the Bangsamoro Local Governance Code of 2023 (BAA 49), nutrition programmes are a mandatory component criterion for any local governance awards and recognition programmes in the BARMM. LGUs are scored on four indicators: activation of Local Nutrition Committees; integration of the LNAP into the AIP; recruitment of Barangay Nutrition Scholars; and hiring of a Registered Nutritionist-Dietitian as Nutrition Action Officer. The MILG with the Commission develops the guidelines and assessment tools.
Section 14 — Not less than ₱15,000,000 is initially appropriated, with succeeding budgets in the annual General Appropriations Act. The budget is transferred directly to the Commission.
Section 15 — The Ministry of Health shall issue implementing rules within 90 days of effectivity.
Section 18 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation.
